case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Federated Publications, Inc v City of Lansing
key_cases.holding: The Court held that FOIA places the burden on the public body to prove an exemption, that exemptions turning on legal determinations are reviewed de novo while discretionary balancing is reviewed for clear error, and remanded for application of the public-interest balancing test.
key_cases.relevance: An oversight body or requester seeking agency records starts from a presumption of disclosure that the agency must overcome.
key_cases.quote: we hold that MCL 15.240(4) of the FOIA specifically places the burden of proof on the public body to show that the public record is exempt from disclosure

key_cases.case_name: Michigan Federation of Teachers & School Related Personnel v University of Michigan
key_cases.holding: The Court held that public employees' home addresses and telephone numbers satisfy both prongs of FOIA's privacy exemption and are exempt from disclosure because releasing them would reveal little or nothing about the conduct of government.
key_cases.relevance: Oversight requests for agency records will be trimmed where the material identifies private individuals rather than agency conduct.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that employees' home addresses and telephone numbers are information of an embarrassing, intimate, private, or confidential nature.

key_cases.holding: The Court vacated a trial court order directing DHS to remove a mother's name from the child abuse central registry, holding that MCL 722.627 vests expunction authority exclusively in the department and that the parent must exhaust the administrative process first.
key_cases.relevance: Registry corrections are an administrative, not judicial, oversight function in Michigan, which shapes where a complaint must be filed.
key_cases.quote: The plain language of the statute grants exclusive jurisdiction to DHS to control expunction from the central registry.

key_cases.case_name: Bradley v Saranac Community Schools Board of Education
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the personnel records of public school teachers and administrators must be disclosed under FOIA because information is of a personal nature only if it reveals intimate or embarrassing details of an individual's private life, and performance appraisals, discipline and complaints about public employment are not.
key_cases.relevance: An oversight request for records showing how public employees performed their public duties is not defeated by the FOIA privacy exemption.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that information is of a personal nature if it reveals intimate or embarrassing details of an individual's private life

key_cases.case_name: Herald Co v City of Bay City
key_cases.holding: The Court held Bay City violated FOIA by refusing to disclose records identifying the final candidates for fire chief, because an application for a public job is not information of a personal nature and its disclosure would not be a clearly unwarranted invasion of privacy, while separately holding that a single city manager is not a public body under the Open Meetings Act.
key_cases.relevance: Herald states the interpretive default for every Michigan records request an oversight body makes: FOIA is prodisclosure and its exemptions are read narrowly against the agency.
key_cases.quote: On its express terms, the FOIA is a prodisclosure statute, and the exemptions stated in § 13 are narrowly construed.

mandatory_reporters: Physicians, dentists, physician's assistants, registered dental hygienists, medical examiners, nurses, and persons licensed to provide emergency medical care — Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.623(1)(a)
Audiologists, psychologists, physical therapists, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and athletic trainers

Marriage and family therapists, licensed professional counselors, social workers, licensed master's social workers, licensed bachelor's social workers, registered social service technicians, and social service technicians
Persons employed in a professional capacity in any office of the friend of the court
School administrators, school counselors, and teachers

MDHHS eligibility specialists, family independence managers, family independence specialists, social services specialists, social work specialists, social work specialist managers, and welfare services specialists — Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.623(1)(b)
Employees of an organization that federal funding statutes, regulations, or contracts would otherwise bar from reporting absent a state mandate — Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.623(1)(c)
Not universal: any other person, including a child, MAY report but is not required to — Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.624
reporting_details: Michigan is not a universal-reporting state: only the professionals and MDHHS employees listed in Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.623(1) must report, and they must report immediately to MDHHS centralized intake by telephone or through the Michigan Online Reporting System. A telephone report must be followed within 72 hours by a written report on form DHS-3200, faxed or emailed to Centralized Intake; a report filed through the online reporting system that contains the information required by Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.623(2) counts as the written report, and MDHHS states that reporting online eliminates the requirement to fill out a DHS-3200 form. Any other person may report voluntarily under Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.624.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: MDHHS centralized intake receives the report
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Mich. Comp. Laws § 722.628(1) requires the department, within 24 hours of receiving a report, to refer it to the prosecuting attorney and local law enforcement or to commence an investigation.
Not specified; MDHHS states CPS has 30 days to complete an investigation unless extenuating circumstances require an extension.
